title: Ulnar neuropathy (5th-digit sensory loss): weak wrist adduction
vignette: A 53-year-old man is evaluated for right hand discomfort. A month ago, the patient started to experience an intermittent pins-and-needles sensation in his right hand that is worse at night. He has no neck pain or history of trauma. The patient has smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for 20 years and has worked as an accountant for the past 30 years. On physical examination, there is loss of sensation over the right fifth digit. There is no swelling, redness, or warmth of the hand. The patient is most likely to have weakness of which of the following movements?

clues.text: pins-and-needles sensation in his right hand that is worse at night
clues.note: Intermittent paresthesias worse at night suggest a compressive/entrapment neuropathy of a peripheral nerve in the hand/wrist.

clues.text: loss of sensation over the right fifth digit
clues.note: Sensory loss over the FIFTH digit (and medial half of the fourth) localizes to the ULNAR NERVE distribution.

whatMatters: Sensory loss over the FIFTH DIGIT localizes to the ULNAR NERVE. The ulnar nerve innervates the FLEXOR CARPI ULNARIS, which produces wrist flexion AND ADDUCTION (ulnar deviation). So ulnar neuropathy weakens WRIST ADDUCTION. Answer D.
strategy: Localize by sensory territory (5th digit = ulnar), then recall the ulnar-innervated forearm muscle: flexor carpi ulnaris -> wrist flexion + ADDuction (ulnar deviation). Reject wrist abduction (radial deviation - flexor carpi radialis [median] + extensor carpi radialis [radial]), wrist extension and elbow extension (radial nerve), and shoulder abduction (axillary/deltoid).

eliminations.label: Elbow extension - radial nerve (triceps)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: extension of the elbow via the triceps. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the triceps is radial-nerve innervated, not ulnar; ulnar injury spares elbow extension. ✅ Correct if: proximal radial nerve injury (crutch/Saturday-night palsy).

eliminations.label: Shoulder abduction - axillary nerve (deltoid)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: abduction of the arm by the deltoid. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the deltoid is axillary-nerve innervated; unrelated to ulnar sensory loss over the 5th digit. ✅ Correct if: axillary nerve injury (anterior shoulder dislocation).

eliminations.label: Wrist abduction - radial deviation (median/radial)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: radial deviation of the wrist by flexor carpi radialis (median) and extensor carpi radialis (radial). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: wrist ABDuction is not primarily ulnar; the ulnar-innervated flexor carpi ulnaris does the opposite (adduction). ✅ Correct if: combined median/radial contribution to radial deviation.

eliminations.label: Wrist extension - radial nerve
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: extension of the wrist by the extensor carpi radialis/ulnaris (radial nerve). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: wrist extensors are radial-nerve innervated; ulnar injury does not weaken wrist extension. ✅ Correct if: radial nerve palsy (wrist drop).

reasoning: Paresthesias worse at night + 5th-digit sensory loss = ulnar nerve involvement
The ulnar nerve innervates the flexor carpi ulnaris in the forearm
Flexor carpi ulnaris produces wrist flexion and ADDuction (ulnar deviation)
-> ulnar neuropathy weakens wrist adduction; answer D
mechanism: The ULNAR NERVE (from the medial cord of the brachial plexus) passes posterior to the medial epicondyle (cubital tunnel) and through Guyon canal at the wrist. It provides sensation to the FIFTH DIGIT, the medial half of the fourth digit, and the hypothenar eminence, and it innervates the FLEXOR CARPI ULNARIS and the medial half of the flexor digitorum profundus in the forearm, plus most intrinsic hand muscles. Because sensory loss localizes here to the fifth digit, the lesion is ULNAR. The flexor carpi ulnaris flexes and ADDUCTS the wrist (ulnar deviation), so ulnar neuropathy weakens WRIST ADDUCTION. (More distal ulnar injury at Guyon canal spares flexor digitorum profundus and produces a more pronounced 'ulnar claw.') The distractors map to other nerves: elbow/wrist extension (radial), shoulder abduction (axillary), and wrist abduction/radial deviation (median flexor carpi radialis with radial extensor carpi radialis).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Anatomy > ulnar nerve: sensation to 5th + medial 4th digit and hypothenar; motor to flexor carpi ulnaris, medial FDP, most intrinsic hand muscles; wrist flexion/adduction; ulnar claw with distal injury.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: 5th-digit sensory loss = ulnar nerve; ulnar drives flexor carpi ulnaris -> wrist adduction.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on ulnar nerve, flexor carpi ulnaris, wrist adduction (ulnar deviation) vs abduction, or Guyon canal? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Elbow/wrist extension = radial; shoulder abduction = axillary; wrist abduction = median FCR + radial ECR.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: ulnar nerve -> flexor carpi ulnaris -> wrist flexion + adduction; sensory 5th digit/hypothenar.

keywords.back: Flexor carpi ulnaris -> wrist flexion + adduction
Flexor carpi radialis (median) + extensor carpi radialis (radial)
More pronounced with distal (wrist) injury (FDP spared)

firstAid.detail: Anatomy: 5th-digit sensory; flexor carpi ulnaris -> wrist adduction.

memoryHook: Pinky numb = ulnar; the ulnar nerve's forearm muscle (flexor carpi ulnaris) pulls the wrist toward the ulna, so lose it and wrist adduction goes weak.
